newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS BEAT SENATORS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS BEAT SENATORS.

text.p: Lyle Odelein's first goal as a Devil, a power-play tally with 8:20 remaining, gave New Jersey its seventh win in eight games, 2-1 over the Ottawa Senators Tuesday.
Odelein was at the bottom of the right faceoff circle when he took a cross-ice pass from Bill Guerin and pushed a shot over goaltender Damian Rhodes' right shoulder.
"We didn't play well," Odelein said. "(Coach) Jacques (Lemaire) told us between periods if we go out and win the third, we win the game. And that's what we did."
Martin Brodeur made 25 saves for the Devils.
In Edmonton, Tony Amonte deflected Alexei Zhamnov's shot past Curtis Joseph with 1:47 left in regulation, lifting the Chicago Blackhawks into a 4-4 tie with the Edmonton Oilers.
Amonte scored twice for Chicago, which battled back from three one-goal deficits to snap its three-game losing streak.

In Pittsburgh, Petr Nedved scored at even strength and on the power play early in the first period and Ken Wregget stopped 34 shots as the Pittsburgh Penguins continued their home dominance over the St. Louis Blues with a 4-2 victory.
Tyler Wright added his first goal of the season for the Penguins.
Defenceman Darius Kasparaitis, acquired Sunday from the New York Islanders, scored into an empty net with 24 seconds remaining to seal the victory.

In Tampa Bay, Corey Schwab made 31 saves for his second career shutout and Rob Zamuner had a shorthanded goal and an assist to help the Tampa Bay Lightning snap a five-game winless streak with a 3-0 blanking of the Los Angeles Kings.
Schwab made 11 saves in the first period.
Daymond Langkow had his first NHL goal for the Lightning.
In Toronto, Wendel Clark scored twice and the Toronto Maple Leafs used a three-goal first period to edge the Buffalo Sabres, 4-3, snapping a four-game losing streak.

Darby Hendrickson and Mats Sundin also scored for the Maple Leafs, who broke an eight-game home winless streak against Buffalo and beat the Sabres in Toronto for the first time since October 19th, 1988.
Clark, who has six goals in his last two home games, scored 89 seconds into the game to put the Leafs ahead to stay.
In Washington, Mark Tinordi scored with 40 seconds left in the third period to lift the Washington Capitals into a 2-2 tie with the Boston Bruins, ending both teams' three-game winning streaks.
Shortly after the Capitals pulled goaltender Jim Carey for an extra attacker, Tinordi jammed a rebound past Bill Ranford for his second goal of the season.
Ranford made 28 saves, including four in overtime.
In Vancouver, Corey Hirsch made 36 saves for his first shutout of the season and Trevor Linden and Markus Naslund scored to lead the Vancouver Canucks to a 2-0 victory over the Dallas Stars.
Hirsch, who had allowed 13 goals in his previous three games, stopped 14 shots in the first period, 12 in the second and 10 in the third for his second career shutout.
Dallas had 11 shots on four power plays in the first period, but could not beat Hirsch.
